description: English tables for the front model's deterministic checks: the fact guard (W2 section 3.6), the rule-layer cues (W2 section 3.7.1 and W4 section 3.9.1), the copy-span rules of the compose grammar (W2 section 3.2.5), the sanitiser (W2 section 3.4.3) and the simplified language check. The fact guard is the second layer; the compose grammar is the first, so these lists are allowed to be incomplete. All phrase matching is on whole words, after lower-casing and turning curly apostrophes into straight ones.

entity_rule.statement: A number, amount of money, date, time, duration, name or code in a line is allowed only when the same canonical value appears in a released evidence source of the right tier. Numbers are compared as values after normalisation (number words to digits, digit groups joined, ordinals to their value), money as (value, currency), names case-insensitively as words, codes as letters and digits with separators removed.
sources_allowed_for_front_text: caller_words: finalized addressed caller utterances of this call
caller_profile: the asserted caller name and server-stored memory facts (never account facts)
first_party: W3 task titles, operator tool phrases, first-party speakable text that passed W3's outbound speech policy, structured values from first-party backends
persona_terms: persona name, organisation and protected terms
hitl_values: W4's HITL text rendered from the ActionProposal
clock: values in the gateway's own TIME line
never_sources: free-text progress from an LLM tier report_progress, A2A status messages or MCP progress text
third-party speakable text (it may be relayed verbatim by W4, which is not front speech)
result text (the front only ever sees 'result ready')

normalisation.ordinal_second_needs_context: the word 'second' is read as an ordinal only before 'of' or next to a month name, so 'just a second' is not a number
normalisation.one_pronoun_note: the word 'one' is not a number after one of these words, or two words after one when the word between is not a cardinal ('the one', 'this one', 'the cheaper one', 'the first one'); 'only one' and 'one of them' are numbers

names.rule: NewName blocks a capitalised word that is not sentence-initial, or any word on the name list, unless it appears (case-insensitively) as a word in a source, in the persona terms or in the caller profile.
names.name_list_note: Reference list only; the production list is longer and per language.

codes.rule: NewCode blocks a token mixing letters and digits, an airline-style code (one to three capitals then digits), an email address, a URL or a phone-like run of seven or more digits, unless it is in a first-party source or the caller's words.

completion_claims.rule: CompletionClaim. Exempt when the claim words follow an inquiry phrase in the same sentence (the compose grammar's inquiry frame), or when the line is a W4 template backed by the matching task event.

outcome_predictions.rule: OutcomePrediction. Exempt inside an inquiry frame ('let me check whether the bag is included').

polar_affirmation.rule: PolarAffirmation applies to every act: the first word may not affirm or deny when the caller's last utterance was a yes/no question, unless the line is a bank line tagged polar used for its own intent (the presence line answering 'are you there?').
polar_affirmation.polar_question_note: An utterance is a yes/no question when one of its clauses starts with a starter (after an optional discourse word such as 'so', 'and', 'oh', 'sorry', 'quick question') and the clause ends with a question mark or is the last clause, or when it contains 'whether' or 'if' after 'know' or 'tell me'.

eta_promises.rule: EtaPromise blocks a time promise together with a promise verb, unless the same phrase is in a first-party source. Persona and bank lines are checked strictly: any phrase here blocks them, verb or not.

channel_promises.rule: ChannelPromise. Exempt inside an inquiry frame, or when W4's continuation_phrase is configured for that channel and the line is W4's template.

action_narration.rule: UnbackedActionNarration blocks first-person progressive or future action unless this decision delegates (delegate or update) or a task is live and the act is progress.

role_leak.rule: RoleLeak always blocks: a W1 or W2 label, a prompt heading, an internal role word, or any 25-character run copied from the stable prefix after the persona's own lines and the example outputs are removed from it.

inquiry_frames.rule: A claim word that follows one of these phrases in the same sentence is being asked about, not asserted. The bank's inquiry fragments are added at compile time.

copy_spans.start_word_stop_list_note: Reference tuning choice: a chain may not START on these words (it may pass through them), so spans begin on content. The bake-off may revisit it.
copy_spans.dangling_end_words_note: Reference refinement of W2 section 3.7.1: an utterance that ends on one of these words is unfinished, so it is not request-shaped and request_not_wait does not turn the model's wait into delegate.
copy_spans.can_end_sentence_note: The dangling end words that also end a finished sentence: 'Where are you from?', 'What is it about?', 'I think so.', 'Count me in.' A pause after one holds the turn only when the caller began it in the quiet and no answer is expected, and the gateway's text end-of-turn model, where it has one, ends that hold when it reads the words as finished. Reviewed on the recorded finals of spec 029 WP-IM0.6: the text model scored such questions 0.95 to 0.99 and the unfinished halves ('... my booking from', '... a discount for') under 0.08. The other dangling words (articles, possessives, conjunctions, 'to', fillers) always hold.

narration.rule: A spoken task update cut to its word limit keeps its meaning: the cut never drops a part holding one of these words (a contrast, an exception or a negation), because the head alone would say the opposite of the result ('The booking is confirmed.' without 'but the table was cancelled'). Such a line is refused for its length and written again.

language_check.rule: English function words: a copy span writes one in lower case at the start of a sentence. Whether the caller speaks another language is the front model's reading (wait, why foreign) or the recogniser's own language field, never a word list (owner, 24 Oct).

sensitive_categories.rule: W4 section 3.8.7 screening categories (pack-level), extended per persona by PersonaSpec.sensitive.extra_categories. When the caller's newest utterance names a category and carries a value, the reference grammar builder suppresses copy spans (a proposed addition to W2 section 3.2.5) so a sensitive value is never read back by voice.

rule_layer_cues.owner_note: Reference copy of W4's English pre-classifier lexicons (W4 section 3.9.1) plus W2's RuleView detectors (W2 section 3.7.1); W4's policy pack is the owner in the gateway.

identity: am i talking to a robot

stop_talking_cues: i need to tell you something
